verdict_reason: S_Nk is exactly Radovanovic et al. 2010's standardized third moment E(N_k - mu)^3/sigma^3 (verified against the fetched JMLR PDF, Sec. 3.2), and the whole pipeline reproduces an independent numpy reference (full stable argsort of cosine, self-masked) at 0.000e+00 on skew, max and top-1% mass over 3 seeds x 2 k values, with Gini agreeing with the pairwise definition to 8.33e-17. Cross-verified against the released scikit-hubness package run locally: BLME's occurrence vector is ELEMENTWISE IDENTICAL (np.array_equal True) to skhubness's own k_occurrence at k = 5, 10 and 50 once skhubness's self-hit is accounted for, and BLME's statistic kernel reproduces skhubness's k_skewness and gini to the last printed digit (0.403241817021 / 0.472377881684 / 0.058680214934 and 0.2157504 / 0.1447088 / 0.0685352). BLME uses the SELF-EXCLUDED convention, which is the one Radovanovic defines ('among the k nearest neighbours of all OTHER points'); skhubness's no-argument score() is the one that is wrong there. Arithmetic is exact across scale: skew/max/gini bit-identical (delta 0.00e+00) from alpha = 1e-40 to 1e+30, invariant to the requested k-set (1.7232808737106582 for k_values [2], [2,7], [2,7,10]) and to batch size (34.071788895 at batch 997/2000/8000 on gpt2).
comparable_reason: Under an iid Gaussian no-hubness null at fixed d = 512, an 8x vocabulary sweep V = 2000 -> 16000 (5 seeds each) moves mean skew only 0.303346 -> 0.319384 (+5.3%), gini 0.175159 -> 0.178195 (+1.7%) and top-1% mass 0.019250 -> 0.019371 (+0.6%) -- but hubness_k10_max rises 21.6 -> 25.2 (+16.7%) and is an unnormalised extreme that spans 49 to 25,598 across the 61 archived models, so it needs a size-matched null and should not be pooled raw. On those 61 models hubness_k10_gini (BLME's stated top-7 predictor) has Spearman rho(d_model) = -0.4315, rho(n_layers) = -0.2602, rho(vocab_size) = +0.3424 and joint rank-OLS R^2 = 0.4611; k10 skew is weaker at rho = -0.2664 / -0.0936 / +0.2013, R^2 = 0.1907.
github_reason: Neither cited paper ships code that I could run: Tomasev's own hubminer is Java (no javac here) and Radovanovic et al. 2010 released none. I cloned and RAN the third-party reference scikit-hubness, whose Hubness estimator implements exactly BLME's statistics: stats.skew(k_occurrence) and gini = sum_ij |x_i - x_j| / (2 n sum x). On 500 unit-norm 32-d points with metric='cosine', BLME's occurrence counts are elementwise identical to skhubness's at k = 5/10/50 modulo skhubness's self-hit (its score() with X=None calls _k_neighbors(X) with start=0, so the self hit is NOT filtered), and BLME's kernel returns skhubness's own numbers exactly. Marked PARTIAL rather than YES because scikit-hubness is a third-party reimplementation, not the code released with either paper.
paper_reason: Radovanovic et al. 2010 footnote 5 publishes six single-realisation S_N5 anchors (n = 10000, k = 5, Euclidean): uniform d = 3/20/100 -> 0.121 / 1.541 / 5.445 and normal d = 3/20/100 -> 0.118 / 2.055 / 19.210. Feeding exact Euclidean 5-NN counts through BLME's statistic kernel over 10 seeds: uniform 0.158576 +/- 0.013793, 1.536223 +/- 0.068358 (rel 0.31%), 5.025845 +/- 0.502066; normal 0.110002 +/- 0.013273, 2.066848 +/- 0.049240 (rel 0.58%), 9.761119 +/- 2.362696. Four of six sit within ~1 SD of the published single realisation; uniform d = 3 is 2.7 SD low and normal d = 100 is 4.0 SD high (both are the heaviest-tailed cases). A self-inclusion convention does NOT explain the d = 3 gap (it moves the mean to 0.187507, further away). PARTIAL also because the shipped configuration is cosine at k = 10/50/100, not Euclidean k = 5, so no shipped output is directly paper-comparable.
confounds_reason: Material but not dominant.
